title: Graph capture consistency for heterogeneous prefill and concurrent replay
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Problem: Our current CUDA-graph capture path assumes uniform prefill shapes and single-stream affinity, which leads to spurious capture invalidations or silent corruption when handling heterogeneous prefill batches (mixed sequence lengths, presence/absence of KV warmups) across concurrent decode streams. Symptoms observed in production: occasional token misordering, KV divergence after replay, and increased recapture frequency under bursty multi-tenant traffic.
background: We rely on CUDA graphs to reduce per-token overheads for stable decode throughput. When prefill inputs vary (different effective seq_len, padding patterns, presence/absence of adapter layers), captured graphs produce incompatible kernel paths or inconsistent KV offsets. Existing mitigations (conservative capture granularity and global locks) increase latency and reduce concurrency. This ticket explores a middle ground: preserve performance benefits while ensuring correctness for heterogeneous prefill shapes and concurrent multi-stream replays.
proposal: 1) Introduce explicit graph "capture fingerprints" that include: canonicalized batch-shape signature, KV cache layout version, and runtime feature flags. 2) Implement shadow KV-copy and compare step after replay in debug builds: replay writes to a shadow buffer and we assert equivalence to CPU/GPU reference for first N tokens. 3) Add replay-fence semantics to isolate concurrent replays that would share ephemeral workspace (preventing KV races). 4) Add adaptive capture segmentation: prefer per-layer segment boundaries when batch heterogeneity detected and fall back to monolithic graphs for homogeneous steady-state. 5) Expose telemetry counters and trace spans for capture mismatches, recapture triggers, and shadow-check failures.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow-copy verification increases memory and slightly impacts latency in debug/qa. Mitigation: enable only for debug, canary nodes, and CI stress tests. Risk: Additional fencing could reduce concurrency. Mitigation: make replay-fence scoped and granular (per-workspace) and measure slot utilization; tune heuristics based on traffic patterns. Risk: Fingerprint explosion leading to cache misses. Mitigation: canonicalize shapes (group by effective token lengths and padding buckets) and cap distinct fingerprints per model to avoid unbounded growth.
acceptance_criteria:
- No correctness regressions on synthetic suite (100k deterministic generation runs) for mixed prefill shapes.
- Shadow-verify detects any KV divergence in CI stress with seeded preemption cases.
- Recapture rate under mixed-batch load reduced by >=40% compared to baseline conservative-capture build.
- Telemetry exposes capture-fingerprint distribution and top-5 mismatch reasons.
- Canary rollout (10% of runtime-1.24 nodes) shows no customer-facing errors for 72 hours under synthetic burst traffic.
tasks: Design capture-fingerprint schema and canonicalization rules
Implement fingerprint generation in capture code path
Add shadow KV buffer and comparator (debug-only) with configurable sample rate
Implement replay-fence primitives and integrate with stream scheduler
Adaptive segmentation: implement heuristics to switch capture granularity
Add telemetry metrics and tracing spans for capture lifecycle
Write deterministic CI tests simulating preemption and mixed-sequence workloads
Run canary: deploy to runtime-1.24 canary pool and monitor for 72 hours
